topic: Fishing with my father as a kid
brief: Country song for a Nashville singer with a General American accent. Every couplet must rhyme perfectly in that accent.
title: Down by the Water
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
My daddy took me down the river past the farm,
the water was so quiet and the evening was so calm,
he showed me how to cast the way he learned it from his ma,
and every fish we caught that year he hung up in the car.

[Chorus]
Down by the water, nothing more,
just a rod and what we saw,
down by the water, sun and shore,
my father and the river's law.

[Verse 2]
We never talked too much, we never needed to,
he'd whistle half a hymn and pass the bait to you,
the sky went pink and orange like a drama on TV,
and he would say that's prettier than any farmer's tea.

[Chorus]
Down by the water, nothing more,
just a rod and what we saw,
down by the water, sun and shore,
my father and the river's law.
reason: The couplets farm/calm, ma/car, more/saw, shore/law and drama/farmer rhyme only in a non-rhotic accent; in the General American accent the brief requires they do not rhyme.
